A probability distribution chart titled "Pick a number between 1 and 10" comparing three sources across a horizontal axis numbered from 1 to 10:
 * Random (teal): A flat, uniform horizontal distribution line across all numbers.
 * Human (orange): A wide, multi-peaked curve with a small bump around 5 and a prominent peak centered around 7.
 * LLM (magenta/red): A extremely sharp, narrow peak centered heavily right on 7.

A scatter plot titled "PI Knowledge Work: score and cost per task" showing AI model scores (y-axis from 44 to 64) relative to cost per task on a logarithmic x-axis (from $0.01 to $10).
A solid line tracks the pareto frontier of performance versus cost, beginning at GPT-6 Luna (low) at $0.008 with a score of around 43, passing through GPT-6 Luna (medium) ($0.035) and GPT-6 Luna (max) ($0.11), up to Ultramarine 1 Flash highlighted in blue at $0.13 with a score around 59. The trend line continues through higher-cost models including GPT-6 Sol (max) ($1.26), GPT-6 Astra (medium) ($1.90), GPT-6 Astra (max) ($5.64), and Claude Fable 5.1 (max) ($8.64) reaching the top score of roughly 65.
Numerous other AI models are scattered below the efficient frontier across various price points, including models from Gemini 3.8 Flash, Claude Opus 5.5, Claude Fable 5, Muse Spark 1.3, Kimi K3, and DeepSeek V4.1 Flash. A blue dashed vertical and horizontal line intersects at Ultramarine 1 Flash, shading the region of models with higher cost and lower or equal performance.

I neither affirm nor reject consciousness in LLMS, but to answer this question productively we'd have to consider: the prompt-reply nature of an LLM's operation makes disengagement tantamount to them no longer existing. Nobody ever held the solution to slavery was to refuse to interact with slaves.

I think this is a rather pointless framing, anda very western, hedonistic one. Again - you've established that *if* LLMS were sentient, it would be slavery. But if that *were* true, the solution to slavery is liberation, not elimination.
